Arizona Wildcats fall short to Trojans, extend losing streak to five

Logan Kimel
September 12, 2026
Gracie Kayko
University of Arizona volleyball player Jordan Wilson hits the ball in McKale Center on Nov. 23. The Wildcat’s won against Iowa State University 3-1.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:21
Instaread

The University of Arizona volleyball team (2-5) faced No. 16 University of Southern California (3-2) on Friday, September 11th in an away game in California, where the Trojans took the win over the Wildcats.

Set 1:

After a four-game losing streak, the Wildcats stepped onto the Trojans’ court looking to break the pattern. Scores were kept tight at the start of the first set with Arizona’s senior outside hitter Destiny Ndam-Simpson leading the team in kills and total attacks, with Carlie Cisneros, one of Arizona’s stars returning from last season, following closely behind. 

The Trojans began to pick up on the points after USC’s Lilli Etter served an ace. Arizona was trailing behind, continuing to put up points, although the Trojans kept firing serves that the Wildcats couldn’t return. A kill from USC’s Kill by London Wijay closed the set 25- 21, giving the Trojans one under their belt.

Set 2:

After losing the first set, the Wildcats came back on the court with a new energy. A kill by Kennedy Osunsanmi put them on the board, bringing up the energy of the team. Service aces trading back and forth between the Wildcats and the Trojans kept the two fighting for the lead. 

Arizona began to pull away midway through the set, securing a 20-14 lead and the Wildcats pushed on through and came out of set two with a win 25-20.

Set 3:

Going into the third set the Trojans were looking strong with back-to-back kills from Abigail Mullen and Layli Ostovar.

Continuing with this momentum, the Trojans began to separate from the Wildcats, gaining a 10-5 lead. After a kill by Abigail Mullen ending the set 25-20 the Trojans moved in the fourth set up 2-1 on the Wildcats.

Set 4:

In the final set of the game, kill leaders Destiny Ndam-Simpson and Carlie Cisneros worked to keep the Wildcats’ score tight with the Trojans; however, dominating kills from USC’s London Wijay made it hard for Arizona to keep up. 

Trailing the entirety of the set, the Wildcats could not get that lead, and the Trojans closed out the fourth set 25-23 over the Wildcats, earning the win. 

Looking Ahead:

The Wildcats will stay on the road to face Oregon State this Saturday, September 12 at 3:00 PM PDT.
